title: 5. Leading Operational KPIs, Structural Potential & CEO Walk-the-Talk
book_title: The KPI Dashboard & Sponsor Accountability: Tracking Error, Liquidity, and Walk-the-Talk

epigraph.quote: A leveraged ETF sponsor cannot control the index, but it is 100% accountable for daily tracking precision, counterparty diversification, and fee discipline.
epigraph.author: ETF Governance & Fiduciary Standard

web_blocks.html: Evaluating operational quality for KORU requires a specialized framework [1][2]. A 3x daily synthetic ETF differs fundamentally from an industrial manufacturer or software enterprise [1]. Rafferty Asset Management does not manufacture memory chips or set Korean monetary policy [1]. Instead, fund operational execution is evaluated across five objective metrics [1][6]. These include Daily Leverage Precision, targeting ~300% gross exposure at each 4:00 PM ET close [1]. They also encompass Swap Financing Spreads and Counterparty Breadth across prime brokers [1]. The remaining three metrics are Collateral Yield Offset, AUM and Secondary Liquidity Scale, and Portfolio Turnover Discipline [1][6].

web_blocks.explanatory_p: KORU's operational plumbing scores strongly across counterparty breadth, swap spreads, and liquidity scaling [1]. In contrast, the Watch flag reflects rate sensitivity of collateral income and multi-year volatility decay [1][5].
web_blocks.takeaway: KPI Health is PASS_WITH_WATCH: Rafferty executes the 3x daily mandate cleanly across four Tier-1 swap dealers, but holder outcomes remain hostage to regime volatility and short-term rate levels [1].

web_blocks.html: On Structural Potential, KORU's upside and downside drivers depend on two structural pillars inside the MSCI Korea 25/50 Index [4]. The first pillar is South Korea's AI and High-Bandwidth Memory (HBM) duopoly [4]. SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics represent approximately 42%–48% of the total index [4]. Global cloud hyperscalers continue expanding capital expenditures into HBM3e, HBM4, and DDR5 enterprise servers [4]. This commercial shift drives high operating leverage and multi-quarter earnings revisions across Seoul [4]. Persistent daily upward trends create an ideal operating environment for 3x daily compounding [1][4]. The second pillar is South Korea's Corporate Value-Up Program [4]. This regulatory effort aims to narrow the persistent valuation discount applied to Korean equities [4]. It incentivizes chaebol affiliates, commercial banks, and industrial leaders to retire treasury shares [4]. It also encourages higher dividend payout ratios and improved return on equity [4].

At the same time, an institutional audit must account for three structural caps on that potential [1][4]. First, the MSCI 25/50 capping rule mechanically trims Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix back toward 25% [4]. It also caps all constituents above 5% at 50% combined during quarterly rebalances [4]. As a result, KORU cannot capture uncapped upside when a single semiconductor leader surges [4]. Second, geopolitical and FX risks on the Korean peninsula remain elevated [1][4]. Macro tensions or export-tariff friction can trigger sharp overnight market gaps [4]. In those events, KRW currency depreciation compounds underlying equity declines inside EWY [1][4]. Third, interest-rate normalization impacts fund economics [1]. If U.S. short-term Treasury yields decline faster than prime broker swap spreads compress, collateral yield contracts [1]. KORU's 44.6% money-market sleeve would generate less interest income [1]. That would reduce its ability to offset the 0.75% advisory fee and the 0.60%–0.85% swap spread [1].

web_blocks.title: Sponsor Walk-the-Talk Audit: Rafferty Asset Management, LLC
paragraphs: 1. Fee Cap Integrity. Rafferty contractually capped operating expenses at 0.95% through September 1, 2026 [1][2]. This cap excludes swap interest, taxes, and acquired fund fees [1][2]. When AUM hovered near $20M–$26M in FY2022–FY2023, Rafferty reimbursed excess fixed expenses [1]. In FY2025, as net assets expanded to $240.60M, the sponsor recouped $35,356 within statutory limits [1]. It also reimbursed $6,893 under Note 6 terms [1].

2. Candid Risk Disclosure. Direxion avoids marketing KORU as a long-term compounder [1][2]. Form N-CSR and the statutory prospectus explicitly warn that annual returns should not suggest long-term holding suitability [1][2]. The sponsor prominently discloses that daily compounding causes multi-day returns to diverge sharply from 3x benchmark returns [1][2].

3. Scale Breakpoints. Note 6 establishes automatic advisory fee step-downs as assets scale [1]. The rate is 0.75% up to $1.5 billion, 0.70% from $1.5B to $2.0B, and 0.55% above $3.0B [1]. At $985.42 million in AUM, KORU remains below the initial $1.5 billion fee breakpoint [1][6].

web_blocks.html: Looking ahead, the single most informative operational KPI is the spread between realized 30-day EWY volatility and directional drift [5]. This metric matters even more than underlying DRAM spot pricing [5]. When EWY annualized volatility holds below ~25% during an upward trend, 3x daily resets add positive compounding momentum [5]. Conversely, when realized volatility exceeds ~40% in a choppy market, quadratic variance drag overwhelms underlying equity gains [5]. Monitoring collateral yield against swap spreads provides a second operational indicator [1]. As of October 2025, government money market funds yielded 3.89%–4.05% [1]. Tracking that yield against swap costs of SOFR plus 60 to 85 basis points reveals net internal fee carry [1].

book_paragraphs: When you evaluate an ordinary operating company, you track same-store sales, gross margins, and customer churn. When you evaluate KORU, you have to build a completely different operational dashboard. You are auditing whether Rafferty Asset Management is running a tight, low-friction derivatives machine—and whether the underlying Korean market structure supports the kind of trending regime where 3x daily leverage works.

Look at the five operational KPIs we pulled from the October 31, 2025 Form N-CSR. First, daily exposure precision: at fiscal year-end, KORU's physical EWY stake plus its four swap contracts delivered roughly 298% effective exposure against its 300% target. Second, counterparty breadth: Rafferty spread $461.65 million of swap notional across four Tier-1 dealers—J.P. Morgan at 45.7%, Citibank at 19.3%, Barclays at 18.1%, and Bank of America Merrill Lynch at 16.9%—so no single bank holds a choke-point over the fund's leverage. Third, swap pricing: spreads ranged from SOFR plus 60 basis points to SOFR plus 85 basis points, competitive institutional terms for emerging-market single-country beta.

Fourth, collateral yield offset: because KORU kept 44.6% of its net assets in Treasury and government money market funds yielding 3.89% to 4.05%, it earned $2.22 million in interest plus $1.59 million in EWY dividends—more than enough to cover its $1.80 million in net expenses and leave $2.00 million in net investment income. Fifth, liquidity scale: net assets climbed from $20.09 million in FY2022 to $240.60 million in FY2025 and $985.42 million by November 2026, with average daily volume reaching 32.57 million shares. Operational execution earns a clear PASS, tempered to PASS_WITH_WATCH only because collateral income depends on short-term U.S. rates and multi-year holders remain exposed to volatility drag.

As for sponsor walk-the-talk, Rafferty Asset Management scores well on candor and contractual discipline. Unlike promoters who quietly bury leverage risks in footnotes, Direxion states upfront in its Form N-CSR that annual return tables 'should not be interpreted as suggesting that the Fund should or should not be held for long periods of time.' When KORU was subscale in FY2022 and FY2023, Rafferty absorbed excess operating costs under its 0.95% expense cap; when AUM surged in FY2025, it recouped $35,356 strictly within its three-year contractual window. The advisory fee schedule even includes step-downs starting at $1.5 billion in assets, though at $985.42 million KORU has not yet crossed that threshold.

If you want to monitor KORU's structural potential going forward without getting lost in daily noise, watch two underlying Korean catalysts and one mathematical gauge. The first catalyst is High-Bandwidth Memory capacity and pricing at SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics, which together drive nearly half of the capped index's weight. The second is Seoul's Corporate Value-Up Program—specifically whether Korean banks, holding companies, and automakers follow through on share cancellations and higher payout ratios that can lift Korea's depressed price-to-book multiples.

The mathematical gauge is the tug-of-war between realized volatility and trend persistence. When South Korean equities trend steadily upward with 20% to 25% annualized volatility, KORU's daily reset compounds in your favor. The moment realized volatility spikes past 40% in a choppy, headline-driven tape—whether from tariff threats, Won swings, or semiconductor inventory scares—variance drag takes over the driver's seat regardless of how cheap Korean stocks look on paper.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good governance in a leveraged ETF does not mean protecting investors from drawdowns—no sponsor can repeal 3x beta or variance math. It means keeping swap spreads tight, diversifying counterparties across four Tier-1 banks, honoring the 0.95% operating cap, and telling the truth in plain English about single-day design. On those criteria, Rafferty walks the talk.

section_takeaway: KORU's operational KPIs rate PASS_WITH_WATCH: Tier-1 swap diversification, ~298% daily precision, and $985.42M AUM liquidity are strong, while collateral rate sensitivity and volatility decay remain structural watch items [1][6].
